subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 13 updates

question: Should the grouped action update wait for the repository-required direct Codex contract inspection, or should the Codex action bump be split from the other twelve updates?
rationale: The patch is mechanically clean, but the review environment could not perform the mandatory direct `../codex` inspection for a security-sensitive action used with API credentials.

options.title: Complete the Codex gate
options.body: Re-run review with direct sibling Codex source access, rebase the PR, and approve the grouped update only after the exact permission and sandbox contract is verified.

options.title: Split the Codex update
options.body: Land the twelve non-Codex action revisions separately and review the codex-action bump with its required dependency-contract evidence.

options.title: Accept the grouped risk
options.body: Merge after current-head checks while explicitly accepting that the repository's direct Codex dependency-inspection gate was not completed.

recommendation.title: Complete the Codex gate
recommendation.body: Re-run review with direct sibling Codex source access, rebase the PR, and approve the grouped update only after the exact permission and sandbox contract is verified.

likelyOwner.reason: The history most strongly connects this person to CI, release, and workflow dependency decisions spanning the affected surfaces.
